status: Implemented and verified for the recorded cases. Overall migration remains active; this is not release approval.

change.cause: pointerDown accepted mouse buttons3/4, registered capture/ownership, then entered drawing or pending-edit paths.
change.fix: Reject mouse button outside0..2 in the initial guard before focus, capture, pointer registration or settle. Reduce owner-mask lookup to the admitted buttons. Sequential code remains inline.
change.onlyProductDifferenceFromDecoderSnapshot: Early mouse-button guard and admitted-owner mask; the other16 recorded product source files are identical.

environmentAttempt.scope: Initial back release navigated to about:blank. Kept as harness-environment evidence, not an application regression count.

No production test hooks or operating-system persistence claims.

actualMacOS.scope: Actual bundled native UI, IPC and isolated filesystem recovery, plus isolated 4096²/32768×1 codec, native quit-ownership and final-scene rendering runs; macOS runs WKWebView. Does not exercise OS file picker dialogs, manual visual acceptance, physical Android or another host platform.

priorEngineSuite.scope: Earlier decoder snapshot; engine and codec sources remain byte-identical. Not rerun for the mouse-only UI admission change.

inputPolicies: Left/right drawing and middle-button pan remain admitted. Touch and pen are outside this mouse-only guard.
A side-button-first chord does not promote a later primary press into a new gesture; a fresh gesture works after all buttons release.
Existing owner-button release handling still closes the stroke when a side button remains held.
Browser back/forward navigation and default focus are not asserted or suppressed by the new guard. CDP clears only test navigation history.
Pen button5 retains existing selected-tool behavior; automatic physical-eraser switching has not been implemented or verified.

Physical Android/Safari web, Windows execution, OS pickers/clipboard/IME, signing/notarization, staging/rollback and remote CI.
